newsitem.title: USA: Oregon Senate to trim back $1.6 bln transit bill.
newsitem.headline: Oregon Senate to trim back $1.6 bln transit bill.

text.p: The Oregon Senate is expected in the coming days to trim back a $1.6 billion state transportation bill that was narrowly approved by the House, lawmakers said on Wednesday.
The House bill would raise a total of $1.6 billion over the next six years, in part from a three cent annual increase in gas taxes over the next three years.
Vehicle registration fees would also increase and a $1.20-a-month telephone tax on each residence and business line would also be instituted under the House plan.
The bill would also increase taxes on large trucks by one-third.
State officials expect the Senate to reduce the annual gas tax increase, lower the increases in registration fees and scrap the telephone tax.

Supporters of the House plan said the funds are urgently needed to improve the state's road system. The House bill passed on a vote of 37-23 late on Tuesday after it had been defeated earlier in the day.
